diagrams.title: The reconstruction questions
diagrams.caption: The boundary problem separates local operations, their representations and their state evaluations. The links are a reading guide to those questions; they do not assert functors or mathematical implications.

diagrams.caption: The unit theorem identifies the stated localizing category through the actual interface. The surrounding questions ask for products, compatible actions and states that an equivalence of linear categories does not specify.

diagrams.title: A full trace and a positive local theory are different targets
diagrams.caption: The arithmetic trace retains the complete divisor. Positivity, normal operations and locality require their own maps. The compact-state comparison supplies another precise example of information lost on taking traces.

diagrams.title: The support detected by consecutive cuts
diagrams.caption: For three ordered labels, the complement of the two separating opens is \(Z_3=\Delta_{13}\). The small diagonal lies inside it; a collision of labels 1 and 3 with label 2 elsewhere defeats both cuts.
hypotheses: Smooth curve; external input order 1,2,3; only consecutive cuts.

witness.conclusion: Both consecutive cuts fail, although the point is outside the small diagonal.

diagrams.title: Bar and cobar retain the ordered operations
diagrams.caption: Connectedness is in arity: the empty coefficient is \(k\). At arity \(n\), more than \(n\) positive factors vanish. This finite bound gives the coherent equivalence without a cohomological boundedness assumption.

nodes.label: Connected counital coaugmented coherent coassociative coalgebras

relations.text: The two functors are inverse equivalences, including the full mapping spaces.
The intrinsic adjunction is \(B\dashv\Omega\); the strict twisting-cochain adjunction has the opposite presentation \(\Omega_{\rm dg}\dashv B_{\rm dg}\).

hypotheses: Smooth separated finite-type curve over a characteristic-zero field.
Ordinary unbounded right differential-module complexes with the consecutive-cut convolution.
Empty coefficient identified with k; all higher associativity and coassociativity data retained.

diagrams.title: Four inflated factors recover an arbitrary source
diagrams.caption: For \(B=Y_{-s}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\), \(s\notin\mathbb Q\), the tower starts at zero and ends at the arbitrary ordinary unbounded complex \(L\). Every displayed two-arrow row is the beginning of a cofiber triangle. The scalar-extension unit \(u\) is distinct from the realization unit \(\eta\).

nodes.description: Inflated from the unrestricted R-complex obtained by derived scalar extension.

hypotheses: \(R=U(\mathfrak{sl}_3)\), \(I=\bigoplus_{w>0}B_w\), and \(F=R\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}-\); \(U\) is inflation.
Both R-actions and two-sided K-flatness are retained.
\(I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}4}=0\), while \(I^{\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}3}\ne0\).

relations.text: Under the separately stated smooth realization hypotheses, invertibility of its actual unit on inflated complexes propagates through this finite tower.

diagrams.title: From a character to an action, and back to the vacuum
diagrams.caption: The complete spaces retain the pointing homotopy and its higher compatibilities. Multiplication followed by vacuum evaluation gives \(\Psi\Theta\simeq1\). The reverse composite is the recognition question; it is proved on the families stated below and remains open for arbitrary admitted actors.

relations.text: \(\Theta\Psi\simeq1\) on the genuinely unital Chevalley family, its specified module extensions, and the nonunital families of Chapter 7.
Full recognition for every pointed factorizing actor, with all roots and refinements.

hypotheses: Characteristic-zero field; the ordered collision category and both tensors specified in Chapter 7.
\(C\) is the Chevalley coalgebra of \(kp_1\oplus kp_2\); \(u\) is an actual coherent pointing.
prohibitions: Do not mark either arrow as a universal equivalence.
Do not identify these spaces with the ordinary exterior-source mapping space.

diagrams.title: The two coproduct paths give the same three-system action
diagrams.caption: The tensor \(\boxtimes_\rho\) includes its cross contraction. The level group need not be commutative. Both paths have the displayed triple value, so coassociativity preserves the order of the levels.
hypotheses: Flat Hopf algebra with bijective antipode over a characteristic-zero coefficient algebra.
Translation, unitary spectral coquasitriangular form and level automorphisms satisfy all displayed identities in Chapter 12.
The fields and all finite products have the specified common rational germs and expansion domains.

diagrams.title: Extension multiplication retains its middle geometry
diagrams.caption: The left map remembers quotient and subobject; the right map remembers the middle object. Pullback along \(p\) followed by the specified pushforward along \(q\) gives the Hall operation. Three-step flags compare its two bracketings.
hypotheses: The constructible-function integral uses finite charge support and an actual domain on which Euler integration is defined.
The coefficient-complex formula is additional data on its specified critical/oriented correspondence; its shifts, supports and orientation roots are retained.
diagrams.status: Defined correspondence; coefficient comparison at its stated family scope

diagrams.title: The full trace and the positive critical trace differ by an exact remainder
diagrams.caption: Both functionals act on the stated arithmetic test algebra. The positive representation counts each real centred zero with its full multiplicity. Equality with the complete Weil functional requires the displayed nonreal contribution to vanish on every test.

edges.label: Trace of the positive critical representation

relations.text: The decomposition is exact on the stated test algebra.

prohibitions: Do not display the remainder as zero.
Do not identify a complex-bilinear residue dual with a positive Hilbert pairing.

diagrams.title: A normalized state, an amplitude line and a filling
diagrams.caption: The two proved constructions begin with different specified finite families and analytic realizations. Their comparison with the state prepared by a geometric filling is open. No arrow identifies a normalized state with an unnormalized amplitude.
